To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the alpha-thrombin receptors in hamster fibroblast cell line CCL39 cells, when activated by a synthetic peptide corresponding to the putative thrombin receptor in the hamster receptor, are able to activate G protein coupled signaling pathways, but are not sufficient to induce mitogenesis.
synthetic peptides corresponding to 5-15 residues of the hamster thrombin receptor activate signal transducing pathways in CCL39 fibroblasts but do not induce mitogenesis.
synthetic alpha-thrombin peptides activate G protein-mediated signaling pathways in CCL39 fibroblasts but do not induce mitogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the mechanisms by which thrombin stimulates mitogenesis in fibroblasts.
the characterization of a novel G protein-coupling mechanism for a peptide receptor, the alpha-thrombin (thrbmbin) receptor.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying thrombin-induced mitogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peptides are not mitogenic, but potentiate DNA synthesis when used in combination with growth factors.
the synthetic alpha-thrombin receptors peptides activate G protein coupled signaling pathways but are not able to induce mitogenesis in the absence of other growth factors.
the thrombin receptor peptide (S-42 to L-55) is a very useful tool for the investigation of the mechanism(s) of thrombin action on cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
synthetic peptides corresponding to a region of the thrombin receptor are agonists of signal transduction pathways in CCL39 hamster fibroblast cells.
the synthetic peptides are not mitogenic but are able to activate G-proteins.
the alpha-thrombin receptors are not mitogenic but potentiate the effects of growth factor receptor tyrosine kinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthetic peptides are not mitogenic by themselves but they can potentiate the mitogenic effect of other factors.
the synthetic peptides are not mitogenic but can be used to probe the signaling pathways activated by the receptor.
the thrombin receptor is not a mitogen.
